record.title: Mining of Fault Propagation Mechanisms in Computer Numerical Control Machine Tools via Information Fusion and Association Rules

publisher_verified_metadata.title: Mining of fault propagation mechanisms in computer numerical control machine tools via information fusion and association rules
publisher_verified_metadata.abstract: Enhancing the reliability of CNC (Computer Numerical Control) machine tools requires precise identification of fault propagation paths. However, existing methods often treat macroscopic topology and microscopic mechanisms in isolation and suffer from biases inherent in single-source data. To address these issues, this paper proposes a reliability-oriented mechanism mining framework integrating information fusion and Association Rule Mining (ARM). First, a game-theoretic weighted Decision Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL)–Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) method is proposed to fuse expert knowledge with failure statistics. This constructs a robust hierarchical topology that mitigates data sparsity. Second, using this topology as a physical constraint, a constraint-based Apriori algorithm is developed. With downtime-centric constraints, it extracts microscopic failure mechanisms from abstract paths. It also overcomes the limitations of traditional algorithms in capturing temporal logic and fault chains. A case study on a five-axis machining center identifies the Electrical System as the most influential subsystem within the identified fault propagation topology and the Automatic Tool Changer (ATC) as the most susceptible unit. The proposed method detects latent High-Impact Low-Probability (HILP) chains and improves Precision, Recall, and F1-score by 2.56 ×, 1.75 ×, and 2.16 × over the traditional algorithm. These results demonstrate improved consistency with the topology-constrained reference patterns for reliability diagnosis of complex electromechanical systems.

record.title: Positioning Road-level Flood Sensing for Disruption Assessment based on Uncertainties and Bayesian Networks

publisher_verified_metadata.title: Positioning road-level flood sensing for disruption assessment under uncertainties using Bayesian networks
publisher_verified_metadata.abstract: Urban flooding severely disrupts road traffic, and assessing these disruptions in a near real-time manner depends on road-level flood sensing that is usually constrained by limited financial and manpower resources. Therefore, positioning a limited number of sensing nodes requires valuing candidate locations. Yet existing strategies value locations mainly by traffic volume or local flood severity rather than disruption, and consider roads in isolation, overlooking how disruption propagates between connected roads. This study builds a double-layered Bayesian network that couples roads through their flood and traffic dependencies. A flood observed at one road then propagates to the inferred traffic disruptions across the connected network. Each candidate location is scored by the Value of Information (VoI) it contributes, combining the magnitude of the revealed traffic disruptions with how far they depart from historical expectation. A greedy algorithm then places sensing nodes where this network-wide value is the greatest. In a New York City expressway case study, the network estimates traffic speeds and the relative levels of disruption, and a few well-placed sensing nodes capture most of the attainable value. The VoI-based positioning achieves higher accumulated value than heuristics based on flood probability, traffic volume, or disruption alone. The framework is expected to help transportation and emergency agencies deploy limited flood-sensing resources where they most improve real-time traffic disruption assessment during urban floods.

record.title: A Novel Data-Model Dual-Driven Implicit Remaining Useful Life Prediction Method for Reusable Thin-Walled Structures

publisher_verified_metadata.title: A novel data-model dual-driven implicit remaining useful life prediction method for reusable thin-walled structures
publisher_verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate remaining useful life prediction for reusable thin-walled structures is challenging because of implicit health indicators and insufficient monitoring data. To address this issue, this study proposes a data-model dual-driven implicit RUL prediction method. First, a distance correlation-based feature mapping method is developed to transform high-dimensional monitoring responses into low-dimensional features that are strongly correlated with implicit load-carrying capacity degradation. Second, a triple-uncertainty adaptive Wiener process is introduced to identify nonlinear degradation trajectories without prespecifying their functional forms, while quantifying random effects, temporal uncertainty, and measurement uncertainty. Subsequently, degradation function-constrained calibration of intrinsic structural parameters is performed, enabling indirect monitoring data to inversely update the high-fidelity structural model. Furthermore, a multi-fidelity Gaussian process model and a discrepancy correction model are employed to predict future structural performance and quantify RUL uncertainty. The results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively captures nonlinear implicit degradation, improves long-term prediction accuracy under limited monitoring data, and provides uncertainty-aware RUL estimates. This method provides an interpretable and physically constrained approach for life prediction and maintenance decision-making of reusable thin-walled structures.

record.title: Decoding the landscape in biomanufacturing of xylose: metabolic bottlenecks and computation-assisted strategies

publisher_verified_metadata.title: Decoding the landscape in biomanufacturing of xylose: metabolic bottlenecks and computation-assisted strategies
publisher_verified_metadata.abstract: As the second most abundant sugar in lignocellulose, xylose suffers from low utilization efficiency due to carbon catabolite repression and the scarcity of natural metabolic pathways. This bottleneck leads to the wastage of nearly 40% of available carbohydrate sources, undermining the economic competitiveness of biorefineries. Overcoming these metabolic barriers is essential for the transition toward large-scale, sustainable biomanufacturing. This review comprehensively summarizes the main pathways of xylose metabolism, with a particular focus on its major metabolic products, rate-limiting enzymes, cofactor preferences, feedback regulation, and compartmentalization. Special attention is given to the significance of modifying rate-limiting enzymes for enhancing carbon flux in the xylose metabolic pathway. The study aims to integrate current knowledge, and to provide support for further research. While enzyme limitations and redox imbalances persist, this review highlights how integrating AI-driven protein engineering with genome-scale metabolic models offers precise solutions. By optimizing key enzymes and correcting cofactor dependencies, these computational strategies provide a robust framework for overcoming metabolic bottlenecks. Ultimately, synergistic AI-metabolic modeling accelerates the efficient conversion of xylose, unlocking its transformative potential for the green bioeconomy.

record.title: A Two-Stage Bayesian Framework for Multi-Fidelity Sequential Updating of Spatial Fragility Fields

publisher_verified_metadata.title: A two-stage Bayesian framework for multi-fidelity sequential updating of spatial fragility fields
publisher_verified_metadata.abstract: This paper develops a Bayesian framework for updating event-conditioned spatial fragility fields by combining physics-informed priors with incrementally available post-disaster observations. The framework supports sequential refinement of regional vulnerability estimates as additional post-disaster evidence becomes available. The framework reformulates physics-informed fragility estimates into a Probit–Normal (PN) representation that captures aleatory variability and epistemic uncertainty in an analytically tractable form. Stage 1 performs local Bayesian updating by moment-matching PN marginals to Beta surrogates that preserve their probability shapes, enabling conjugate Beta–Bernoulli updates with soft, multi-fidelity observations. Fidelity weights encode source reliability, and the resulting Beta posteriors are re-projected into PN form, producing heteroscedastic fragility estimates whose variances reflect data quality and coverage. Stage 2 assimilates the heteroscedastic pseudo-observations through an ordered probit-warped Gaussian Process (GP) that propagates information across space and structural archetypes. A shared latent spatial severity field and strictly positive threshold-gap functions enforce pathwise ordering of exceedance probabilities and yield nonnegative exact damage-state probabilities. The framework is applied to the 2011 Joplin tornado, where wind-field priors and computer-vision damage assessments are fused under varying assumptions about tornado width, sampling strategy, and observation completeness. Controlled synthetic experiments and the Joplin application show that the framework can reduce the influence of biased priors as evidence accumulates, propagate locally updated information into unobserved regions, and produce uncertainty-aware, ordinally valid exceedance and exact damage-state probability fields.

record.title: A two-stage deep causal inference method with association prior for urban rail transit risk impact deduction and proactive intervention

publisher_verified_metadata.title: A two-stage deep causal inference method with association prior for urban rail transit risk impact deduction and proactive intervention
publisher_verified_metadata.abstract: To enhance the in-time safety management capability of urban rail transit, this paper proposes a two-stage deep causal inference framework with association prior for causal discovery and interpretable intervention in risk impact deduction. Firstly, the association rules obtained by the improved W-apriori algorithm are transformed into prior matrix, allowing causal weight to be estimated in the feasible risk evolution space and bridging the gap between statistical mining and causal inference. Next, a five-layer causal topology is reconstructed using AP-DAG-GNN, with high-weight causal relationship extracted by Pareto optimization. Then, Causal-DEMATEL and DWBC are designed to analyze node-level topological features and path-level causal cascades. Moreover, event-specific causal attribution is developed for interpretable analysis of individual high-risk emergency, identifying key causal evolution pathways and intervention nodes. To demonstrate the proposed framework, six event types are simulated using real operational data from Beijing Metro combined with baseline comparison, ablation experiment and structural stability analysis, which indicates that high-weight causal topology selected by Pareto is sensitive to random optimization and finite sample perturbations, while some key causal relationships exhibit relatively high recurrence and node importance ranking exhibits a certain degree of event dependency. These findings can not only support the effectively identification of stable risk propagation pathways and candidate intervention priorities, but also sensitively capture causal center shifts caused by specific conditions, thereby providing a foundation for early intervention, warning release, and implementation of proactive risk prevention and control strategies.

record.title: Design of robust multiple-layer networks for unmanned aerial vehicle communication systems

publisher_verified_metadata.title: Design of robust multiple-layer networks for unmanned aerial vehicle communication systems
publisher_verified_metadata.abstract: A multiple-layer UAV system includes multiple types of UAVs, and different types of UAVs are at different layers. Network robustness is used to measure the connectivity of remaining network after some nodes fail. A highly robust network can ensure that UAVs can still communicate with each other even after some UAVs fail. To improve robustness of multi-layer UAVs network, we propose a method that combines positions of UAVs and network topology. The method can be divided into two sub-methods: flight strategy and network structure. In the flight strategy, an intra-layer potential field and an inter-layer potential field are used to adjust positions of UAVs under constraints, which can reduce distance between UAVs and can enable UAVs to establish more links. Although increasing links can improve the robustness of network, the dependence of network on critical nodes has greatly increased. Once these nodes fail, the robustness of network sharply decreases. In the network structure, Deep learning method is used to search for highly robust network structure. The designed deep learning method can evenly distribute links across nodes while increasing links, thereby reducing the impact of critical nodes on network. In 3D space, experimental results show that our method can meet constraints of multi-layer UAVs network, and enables networks to have high robustness in multiple failure modes.

record.title: ContextMRI: Enhancing compressed sensing MRI through metadata conditioning

publisher_verified_metadata.title: ContextMRI: Enhancing compressed sensing MRI through metadata conditioning
publisher_verified_metadata.abstract: Compressed sensing MRI seeks to accelerate MRI acquisition processes by sampling fewer k-space measurements and then reconstructing the missing data algorithmically. The success of these approaches often relies on strong priors or learned statistical models. While recent diffusion model-based priors have shown great potential, previous methods typically ignore clinically available metadata (e.g. patient demographics, imaging parameters, slice-specific information). In practice, metadata contains meaningful cues about the anatomy and acquisition protocol, suggesting it could further constrain the reconstruction problem. In this work, we propose ContextMRI, a text-conditioned diffusion model for MRI that integrates granular metadata into the reconstruction process. We train a pixel-space diffusion model directly on minimally processed, complex-valued MRI images. During inference, metadata is converted into a structured text prompt and fed to the model via CLIP text embeddings. By conditioning the prior on metadata, we unlock more accurate reconstructions and show consistent gains across multiple datasets, acceleration factors, and undersampling patterns. Our experiments demonstrate that increasing the fidelity of metadata — ranging from slice location and contrast to patient age, sex, and pathology — systematically boosts reconstruction performance. This work highlights the untapped potential of leveraging clinical context for inverse problems and opens a new direction for metadata-driven MRI reconstruction. Code is available at https://github.com/DoHunLee1/ContextMRI.

record.title: All-magneto-dielectric metasurface with Ultrathin and Ultra-broadband Electromagnetic Absorption

publisher_verified_metadata.title: All-magneto-dielectric metasurface with ultrathin and ultra-broadband electromagnetic absorption
publisher_verified_metadata.abstract: Achieving ultrabroadband electromagnetic-wave (EMW) absorption with a low profile remains a major challenge for next-generation stealth and electromagnetic-compatibility applications. Here, we develop an all-magneto-dielectric metasurface (AMDM) that synergistically combines intrinsic material loss with evanescent-wave control. FeSiCr@PVB composites with tunable dielectric and magnetic properties are first optimized to balance impedance matching and attenuation capability. Subsequently, a periodic metasurface structure is introduced to further regulate wave propagation, enabling enhanced absorption through evanescent mode excitation and near-field energy localization. Genetic algorithm optimization is employed to achieve global structural optimization, resulting in a metasurface exhibiting an ultra-broadband effective bandwidth from 1 to 24 GHz with a relative bandwidth of 184%. Full-wave simulations and experiments show consistent broadband RCS reduction. This work provides a viable strategy for decoupling and independently optimizing absorption mechanisms across different frequency regimes, offering new insights into the design of ultrathin, ultra-broadband EM absorbers.

record.title: Risk response decisions for critical infrastructures in complex interdependent scenarios: A data-intelligence-driven integrated model

publisher_verified_metadata.title: Risk response decisions for critical infrastructures in complex interdependent scenarios: A data-intelligence-driven integrated model
publisher_verified_metadata.abstract: Critical infrastructures (CIs) are often exposed to multiple risks whose consequences may be aggravated or mitigated by both CI interdependency and risk interdependency, making the modeling of risk response decisions (RRDs) more challenging under limited and heterogeneous information. This study aims to develop a data-intelligence-driven RRD model that links preparedness, detection/diagnosis, and treatment decisions through a shared ontology representation. First, an RRD ontology is constructed from multi-source text data and expert knowledge to organize reusable scenario, criterion, strategy, and rule knowledge. Subsequently, a dual-interdependency and criterion-adaptive mechanism is employed to quantify the realistic scenario by combining predefined information with on-site observations and interdependency-effect information, in which aggregation is configured according to the interdependency and cumulative characteristics of individual criteria. Following the scenario diagnosis, ontology-based case retrieval is conducted, and the extracted strategies enter a rule-guided post-retrieval adaptation process involving effect screening, coverage checking, and strategy coordination. Furthermore, a case study on the “7.21 Beijing Torrential Rain” is conducted. Sensitivity, ablation, and retrospective analyses examine the local stability of the decision results, the effects of interdependency modeling and rule-guided adaptation, and the correspondence between generated actions and documented historical responses. This study provides case-specific evidence for the feasibility, incremental decision value, and practical relevance of the proposed model for RRDs in complex interdependent CI scenarios.

record.title: DERF: Dynamic evolution risk field-based risk assessment for pedestrian-vehicle potential collision

publisher_verified_metadata.title: DERF: Dynamic evolution risk field-based risk assessment for pedestrian-vehicle potential collision
publisher_verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate and timely assessment of pedestrian-vehicle collision risk is fundamental to the reliability and safety assurance of autonomous driving systems. In urban traffic, inadequate modelling of pedestrian-vehicle interactions and lagging risk perception leave pedestrians vulnerable. To address this, the paper introduces a dynamic evolving risk field (DERF) method and develops a collision volume model using bounding boxes to enable effective trajectory crossing detection. Temporal risk is quantified by fusing time difference to collision and time to last arrival, while spatial risk is modelled via cusp catastrophe theory to capture nonlinear transitions from gradual to acute states. A multilayer perceptron nonlinearly fuses these features into spatiotemporal interaction factors, combined with a direction-sensitive modulation function, enabling real-time smooth evolution of risk field intensity and distribution. Experiments on the pedestrian-vehicle interaction dataset show that our method achieves 0.92 accuracy at a 1 s prediction horizon and 38.5 FPS, outperforming state-of-the-art in accuracy, recall, and operation speed. The results confirm that our approach delivers reliable risk estimates with balanced precision and recall, supporting reliable safety assessment under dynamic and uncertain traffic conditions.
